extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, USPTO disciplinary practitioners, and OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the notice/response process, publication/notice obligations, conditions for reinstatement, and examples of attorney misconduct that support discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24; a Notice and Order is sent and the respondent is given an opportunity to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on the reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and Order provided the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). If the respondent fails to file a response, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and impose reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (predicate: being suspended from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State) is a ground for suspension from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order suspended the respondent for four years for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being suspended from the practice of law by a State authority; the Office's disciplinary action mirrors the state disciplinary sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reinstatement to practice before the USPTO requires that the OED Director grant a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement can be conditioned on compliance with terms of the state order — here, the respondent's reinstatement was conditioned on payment of restitution to the complainant as set forth in the state's Final Judgment and Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties during suspension per 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner must comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs the respondent to comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (the Order does not reproduce those duties but mandates compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations (FOIA Reading Room, Official Gazette, and 37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order electronically at OED's FOIA Reading Room and publish a Notice in the Official Gazette; notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 must be given to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific publication actions in this Order: (1) electronically publish the Final Order at OED's FOIA Reading Room; (2) publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette containing name, registration number, jurisdiction, basis and length of suspension, reinstatement conditions, and summary of underlying findings; (3) give notice under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO customer numbers/electronic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), if any, upon suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly commands dissociation of the suspended practitioner's name from customer numbers and verified electronic system accounts to prevent continued use while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney misconduct examples that support discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific misconduct findings that supported the state suspension and formed the predicate for USPTO discipline: receiving funds from clients to pay USPTO patent application fees but failing to make required payments (resulting in abandonment), failing to timely advise clients of abandonments or failures to make payments, commingling client funds with business/personal funds, failing to adhere to trust account rules, and falsely representing maintenance of professional liability insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Presiding Disciplinary Judge found these facts (e.g., in approximately 46 cases the respondent failed to make required payments), the respondent admitted violations in an Agreement for Discipline by Consent, and was found to have violated specific state professional conduct rules (A.R.S. Sup. Ct. Rule 42, E.R. 8.4(c) for dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation, and A.R.S. Sup. Ct. Rule 43 regarding trust accounts). Such factual misconduct can justify reciprocal discipline by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural form and delivery of Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order in this case was sent by certified mail and included a certified-mail receipt number; it specified the 40-day response deadline and was considered delivered on a particular date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This demonstrates procedural practice: issue a Notice and Order by certified mail (record receipt), state the statutory response period (40 days), and note delivery date — failure to respond within the period supports a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content elements for a Notice of Suspension publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Suspension published in the Official Gazette included the suspended practitioner's name, city and state, registration number, description that the action was a reciprocal disciplinary proceeding, duration of suspension, statutory/regulatory basis (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), and conditions of reinstatement including restitution requirements and a summary of the underlying state findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing a suspension notice, include identifying information (name, registration number, jurisdiction), the legal basis and duration of discipline, reinstatement conditions, summary of underlying misconduct/findings, and links to where the full disciplinary decision is publicly available (e.g., FOIA Reading Room).
